topic: K1 Fix a positive dominated ADMG nested-Markov model with a finite complete list of ordinary and post-fixing Verma constraints and an identified smooth causal functional. K2 characterize exactly when the closure of the sum of residualized weighted-moment spaces equals the full tangent-space orthocomplement, including a compatibility characterization when equality fails. K3 derive the canonical gradient and efficiency bound and construct an alternating-projection or sieve one-step estimator whose rate tracks subspace angle and nuisance error. K4 prove the semiparametric convolution lower bound and quantify efficiency lost by incomplete constraints. Use the anchor's smallest continuous two-Verma graph and Ananke as the witness and consumer.

open_problems.open_problem: For a positive dominated ADMG with finitely many ordinary and post-fixing Verma constraints, when is the full tangent-space orthocomplement exactly the closed sum of the residualized weighted-moment spaces, and what compatibility defect characterizes failure of equality?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves the residualized weighted-moment characterization for one nested-Markov constraint, obtains only a subspace for multiple constraints, and explicitly leaves the complete multi-constraint characterization open.
source_refs.author: Razieh Nabi, Anna Guo, Lin Liu

source_refs.claim: The complete orthocomplement result concerns Markov models defined solely by ordinary conditional-independence restrictions, not post-fixing Verma constraints.
source_refs.author: Trung Phung, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: Nested-Markov constraints are conditional independences in kernels reached by fixing, so simultaneous derivatives contain coupled density-ratio terms absent from ordinary observed-law CI models.
source_refs.author: Thomas S. Richardson, Robin J. Evans, James M. Robins, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.excerpt: It is not the semiparametric efficiency bound for the full conditional-moment DDD model.
Benchmark the joint estimator against the semiparametric DDD efficiency bound, or prove a precise condition

open_problems.why_unsolved: Nabi, Guo, and Liu prove only the inclusion generated by summing individual residual spaces. Equality requires a local range result for the combined fixing map and proof that separately valid residual perturbations paste into one regular score; fixing couples the derivatives through density ratios, and their ranges may overlap incompatibly or have a nonclosed sum. Phung and Shpitser's ordinary-CI projection proof does not treat those terms. The banked DDD proposal independently warns that optimizing in a retained moment span need not reach the full conditional-moment bound, while the data-fusion proposal shows that separately feasible restrictions need an explicit compatibility certificate. The missing object is therefore a bounded right inverse, split constant-rank theorem, or exact range/cokernel condition for the combined derivative.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving equivalent closed-range, bounded-right-inverse, and residual-compatibility conditions for F=(F_1,...,F_J), proving T(P)=intersection_j ker DF_j(P) and T(P)^⊥=closure(sum_j range DF_j(P)^*), with an explicit annihilator or cokernel certificate when equality fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from hidden-variable graphical equality constraints to Hilbert-space efficiency geometry and ends at the unresolved multi-constraint boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent-variable DAGs impose Verma constraints beyond ordinary CI -> fixing turns one constraint into weighted L2 orthogonality -> several fixing constraints currently give only a subspace -> exact joint geometry and compatibility are required

method_exemplars.technique: Express ordinary-CI tangent orthocomplements as residualized conditional-moment spaces and prove completeness by conditional-expectation projections.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest complete multi-restriction orthocomplement proof; the required transfer replaces ordinary conditional expectations by coupled post-fixing derivative-adjoint operators.

method_exemplars.technique: Use conditional-moment score operators and optimal instruments to characterize information through the range of the adjoint operator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Verma residual spaces are weighted conditional-moment ranges, so operator-range duality is the natural route from the combined derivative to the full orthocomplement and efficiency bound.

method_exemplars.technique: Use nested-Markov coordinates and algebraic geometry to prove completeness of observed equality constraints in finite discrete latent-DAG margins.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest completeness argument, while making clear that a dominated-L2 right inverse or compatibility theorem is an additional analytic step.

open_problems.open_problem: On the smallest positive continuous two-Verma ADMG, is every mean-zero L2 score in the common kernel of the ordinary and post-fixing derivatives integrable to a regular nested-Markov submodel, or does an explicit nonintegrable common-kernel score exist?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves equality completeness and regular dimension for finite discrete nested-Markov models, not path integrability for continuous dominated laws.
source_refs.author: Robin J. Evans

source_refs.claim: The paper derives dominated-L2 tangent restrictions from post-fixing weighted moments but leaves the complete joint tangent-space characterization open with multiple nested constraints.
source_refs.author: Razieh Nabi, Anna Guo, Lin Liu

source_refs.claim: The fixing calculus characterizes reachable kernels and nested factorization but does not establish Banach-manifold regularity or continuous-score path integrability.
source_refs.author: Thomas S. Richardson, Robin J. Evans, James M. Robins, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.excerpt: State and prove the precise algebraic relation between V(I_m), the closure of the compatibility projection
The exact real information-order frontier, the real feasible atlas ... remain open.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Finite-state polynomial completeness does not imply that the continuous fixing map is a split submersion in dominated L2. Differentiating all fixing identities produces a formal common kernel, but a path with such a score must simultaneously preserve positivity, normalization, density-ratio denominators, and the nonlinear joint fixing identities. The banked LiNGAM work identifies the analogous gap between algebraic closure and realizability by real feasible laws. In the nested-Markov model this becomes a local-submodel construction or second-order obstruction problem, and a counterexample would kill the proposed tangent description before any projection or efficiency calculation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a local-submodel theorem integrating a bounded dense subclass of intersection_j ker DF_j(P) and identifying its L2 closure with the tangent space, or a concrete positive continuous two-Verma law and common-kernel score with a regime-level proof of nonintegrability.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing separates completeness of equality constraints from the harder geometry of latent-variable models, which cleanly exposes the continuous regularity boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent-DAG margins have difficult equality constraints -> finite discrete nested-Markov coordinates capture all equalities -> semiparametric efficiency for dominated continuous laws additionally requires every linearized score to arise from a regular positive path

method_exemplars.technique: Construct identifiable nested-Markov coordinates and use Jacobian rank and algebraic completeness in the finite discrete model.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A continuous proof must replace finite coordinates and polynomial rank by local coordinates or a right inverse for dominated kernels, exactly the step needed to integrate scores.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct reachable kernels by fixing sequences and prove order invariance and equivalence of nested factorization formulations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those nonlinear fixing identities are precisely what a candidate score path must preserve beyond first order.

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate weighted post-fixing moment identities in L2 and residualize their representers.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the candidate common kernel whose equality with the genuine continuous-model tangent space must be proved or refuted.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a cross-fitted sieve or alternating-projection one-step estimator for a smooth identified causal functional under multiple Verma constraints attain an angle-aware limit theory when the residual spaces are nuisance-estimated and their generalized Friedrichs angle may vanish?

source_refs.claim: The paper gives population projection and minimum-variance characterizations under Verma constraints but no multi-constraint, angle-aware estimator or projection-rate theorem.
source_refs.author: Razieh Nabi, Anna Guo, Lin Liu

source_refs.claim: Cyclic projections across several closed Hilbert subspaces converge quickly when the generalized Friedrichs number is below one and can converge arbitrarily slowly otherwise.
source_refs.author: Catalin Badea, Sophie Grivaux, Vladimir Muller

source_refs.claim: Sieve minimum distance for conditional-moment models can attain semiparametric efficiency and asymptotic normality under explicit sieve and nuisance-rate conditions.
source_refs.author: Chunrong Ai, Xiaohong Chen

source_refs.claim: Ananke implements graphical identification and existing parametric and semiparametric estimators but not multi-Verma tangent projections or angle-adaptive stopping.
source_refs.author: Jaron J. R. Lee, Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.excerpt: derive a local-to-nullspace phase theorem for the plug-in quotient diagnostic
Rewrite Conjecture 2 with a fully specified theta estimator, variance estimator, joint Gaussian limit

open_problems.why_unsolved: The nested-Markov anchor stops at a population Hilbert projection, whereas deterministic alternating-projection theory assumes known closed subspaces and becomes arbitrarily slow as their generalized angle degenerates. Here every projection is estimated through post-fixing density ratios and conditional regressions, so the first proof step must replace a deterministic product-of-projections bound by a cross-fitted perturbation bound whose error is amplified by the angle. The archived proximal-quotient run left even its fixed-rank local-to-nullspace Gaussian phase unproved. No searched work combines multiple Verma derivatives with nuisance-estimated subspaces, angle-dependent stopping, and one-step inference.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit sieve or cyclic-projection one-step estimator with a stochastic expansion, an iteration-and-perturbation error bound in the generalized Friedrichs angle, sufficient joint conditions on sieve bias, nuisance products, stopping error, and angle decay for root-n asymptotic normality, and a consistent efficiency-bound estimator.

writing_exemplar.why: Its population projection formulation provides the cleanest arc from exploitable Verma information to a computable multi-constraint estimator.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Verma constraints restrict the tangent space -> canonical gradients are population projections away from residual spaces -> Ananke needs estimated projections -> near-aligned spaces require angle-aware iteration, nuisance control, and inference

method_exemplars.technique: Control cyclic products of orthogonal projections by a generalized Friedrichs number and prove the quick-uniform versus arbitrarily-slow convergence dichotomy.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired gradient is obtained relative to several residual spaces, so this is the deterministic angle-dependent core that must be stabilized under estimated projections.

method_exemplars.technique: Approximate conditional-moment components by sieves, use optimal weighting, and prove root-n normality and efficiency by controlling approximation and nuisance errors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Post-fixing Verma restrictions are weighted conditional moments, so their residual spaces admit the same growing-instrument architecture once angle amplification is added.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive influence-function estimators mechanically for identified ADMG functionals and establish robustness and efficiency in tractable graph classes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the causal-functional nuisance expansion and Ananke-compatible substrate; the new move is subtracting the fully estimated multi-Verma orthocomplement projection.

open_problems.open_problem: For a smooth causal functional in a multi-Verma nested-Markov model, what is the semiparametric convolution lower bound, and what exact variance-gap formula and strictness conditions quantify efficiency lost when only an incomplete constraint subfamily is used?

source_refs.claim: The paper characterizes efficiency by projection for a single Verma constraint but has only a subspace of the orthocomplement with multiple constraints, so the resulting bound need not be the full-model bound.
source_refs.author: Razieh Nabi, Anna Guo, Lin Liu

source_refs.claim: The paper links tangent-space calculations and canonical gradients to information bounds for regular semiparametric estimators.
source_refs.author: Whitney K. Newey

source_refs.claim: Projection onto ordinary graphical-independence restrictions improves estimation of causal bound endpoints, showing that omitted graphical restrictions can have a measurable variance cost.
source_refs.author: Ting-Hsuan Chang, Caleb H. Miles, Ilya Shpitser, Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen, Daniel Malinsky

source_refs.excerpt: It is not the semiparametric efficiency bound for the full conditional-moment DDD model.
Constructing and validating one procedure that adapts honestly through equality remains open.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A convolution bound must use the genuine tangent space, not merely a known subspace of its orthocomplement. If S is the span of the restrictions used and S is strictly smaller than T(P)^⊥, projecting a baseline influence function off S is valid but may be inefficient; existing nested-Markov work does not identify the missing component for coupled constraints. The banked DDD run makes the same retained-span versus full-bound distinction, and the banked transport run shows that degeneracy can destroy a uniform first-order Gaussian pivot. The missing steps are LAN along jointly constrained regular submodels, nested-projection geometry, and control of local sequences where either the constraint-space angle or incremental variance gain vanishes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A full-versus-reduced-model convolution theorem, an identity Var(D_incomplete)-Var(D_eff)=‖Π_{T(P)^⊥∩S^⊥}D_0‖² with necessary and sufficient zero-loss and strict-loss conditions, and a regime statement describing attainable or impossible uniform efficiency as the angle or gain degenerates.

writing_exemplar.why: It treats Verma constraints as statistical information and projection as the source of efficiency gains, making the cost of omitted constraints the natural destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Hidden-variable graphs impose testable equality information -> tangent projection converts that information into lower variance -> an incomplete multi-constraint projection may discard information -> quantify the exact loss and prove the corresponding lower bound

method_exemplars.technique: Calculate semiparametric information bounds from tangent spaces and connect canonical gradients to limiting distributions of regular estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the full multi-Verma tangent space is established, this is the direct route to the requested convolution lower bound.

method_exemplars.technique: Project influence functions onto graphical-constraint tangent spaces and construct estimators realizing the variance improvement.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives a causal graphical example where extra equality restrictions reduce variance; the new target replaces ordinary CI projections by post-fixing residual spaces and compares complete with incomplete projection.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive influence functions and attaining estimators for identifiable hidden-variable graphical targets in tractable observed-data models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies baseline influence functions for ADMG causal targets against which complete and incomplete Verma variance reductions can be measured.

literature_map:
Nabi, Guo, and Liu (2026, arXiv:2608.24602) is the exact anchor: one Verma constraint is complete, while multiple constraints yield only a known subspace of the orthocomplement.
Phung and Shpitser (2026, UAI, arXiv:2607.23439) characterize orthocomplements for ordinary-CI Markov models and do not cover fixing-derived Verma constraints.
Richardson, Evans, Robins, and Shpitser (2023, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1701.06686) establish fixing, reachable kernels, nested factorization, and the graphical source of Verma constraints.
Evans (2018, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1501.02103) proves algebraic equality completeness for finite discrete observed variables, not continuous dominated constant rank or score integrability.
Shpitser, Richardson, Robins, and Evans (2012, arXiv:1207.5058) develop discrete fitting and structure learning for nested-Markov models, not continuous semiparametric tangent geometry.
Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (2022, JMLR, arXiv:2003.12659) connect ADMG identification and influence-function estimation but treat graph classes with tractable observed-law equality structure.
Lee, Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (2023, arXiv:2301.11477) make Ananke a natural consumer; its published scope has identification and semiparametric estimation but no multi-Verma projector.
Chamberlain (1987, Journal of Econometrics, DOI:10.1016/0304-4076(87)90015-7) provides the conditional-moment operator and optimal-instrument foundation.
Ai and Chen (2003, Econometrica, DOI:10.1111/1468-0262.00470) give efficient sieve estimators for conditional-moment models under explicit approximation and nuisance-rate conditions.
Badea, Grivaux, and Muller (2012, St. Petersburg Mathematical Journal, arXiv:1006.2047) tie cyclic-projection rates to generalized Friedrichs angles and permit arbitrarily slow convergence.
Newey (1990, Journal of Applied Econometrics, DOI:10.1002/jae.3950050202) supplies the general tangent-space efficiency-bound framework.
Chang, Miles, Shpitser, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and Malinsky (2026, arXiv:2605.11515) use ordinary graphical-independence projections to improve causal-bound estimation, not post-fixing constraints.
The central tension is that graphical equality completeness, L2 derivative completeness, common-kernel path integrability, computability of the full projection, and attainability of its convolution bound are distinct steps.
Focused searches found no paper combining multiple Verma fixing derivatives with exact compatibility, vanishing-angle estimated-projection rates, or a complete-versus-incomplete constraint efficiency-loss theorem.
